issues.legal_issue: A tenant obtains the one-time protection against eviction for rent default only when an order for possession is not made because the tenant complied with the rent-payment order; compliance in an earlier proceeding that the landlord withdrew does not itself amount to obtaining that protection.
material_facts: In an earlier eviction proceeding based partly on rent default, the tenant complied with an order to pay or deposit the arrears.
The landlord withdrew that proceeding because of a procedural defect, namely the absence of a notice to quit; the proceeding was not terminated because compliance prevented an order for possession.

The landlord later brought another eviction proceeding based on rent default, and the Rent Controller refused to give the tenant the protection again on the basis that it had already been obtained in the earlier proceeding.
issues.conclusion: The tenant had not obtained the protection in the earlier proceeding because that proceeding was withdrawn rather than concluded with possession denied on account of the tenant’s compliance. The tenant was therefore entitled to claim the protection in the later proceeding, subject to depositing the arrears as directed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 14(2) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, read with its proviso, the benefit is immunity from an order for possession on the ground of rent default, not merely the passing of an order under section 15(1). Section 15(1) requires the Controller to give the tenant the facility to pay or deposit rent, and section 15(6) provides that compliance prevents an order for possession on the ground of default. The proviso applies only where possession was not ordered because the tenant complied; a landlord’s withdrawal of an earlier proceeding does not establish that benefit. The Court approved Rama Gupta v. Rai Singh Kain and Ashok Kumar v. Ram Gopal, and referred to Kahan Chand Makan v. B.S. Bhambri while rejecting its broader approach insofar as it conflated the section 15 facility with the section 14(2) benefit.

rule.if: rent_default_eviction_case and prior_rent_payment_order_complied_with and prior_case_withdrawn_by_landlord and not prior_possession_order_prevented_by_compliance

predicates.rent_default_eviction_case: The proceeding seeks possession on the ground that the tenant defaulted in paying rent.
predicates.prior_rent_payment_order_complied_with: In an earlier proceeding, the tenant complied with an order to pay or deposit rent.
predicates.prior_case_withdrawn_by_landlord: The landlord withdrew the earlier proceeding rather than obtaining a final decision on the possession claim.
predicates.prior_possession_order_prevented_by_comp: The earlier proceeding ended without an order for possession because the tenant’s compliance with the rent-payment order prevented that order.

issues.definition: When a rent-default possession proceeding follows an earlier proceeding in which the tenant complied with a rent-payment order but the landlord withdrew the case, and compliance did not prevent an order for possession, the tenant may claim the rent-default protection.
